A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MotionLab with the same authors, framework and principal benchmarks. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation and editing results, specialist comparisons and component ablations in Section 6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v4 retains original benchmark experiments and reports additional keyframe-count and task-combination comparisons in Appendices A and B.

M1.justification: The MotionFlow Transformer, Aligned ROPE, instruction modulation, curriculum sequence and CFG procedures remain unchanged. 'Condition Path' becomes 'Modality Path'; the rewritten pre-training discussion clarifies joint-coordinate masking already described in v1 Section 5.3.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanML3D, its style-transfer subset and MotionFix for the same generation and editing tasks. The added keyframe-count and task-combination experiments vary controls within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 3-5 retain their comparator sets, and the CondMDI in-betweening and MCM-LDM style-transfer comparisons persist. The specialist models labeled explicitly in v4 were already evaluated as 'Ours*' in v1 Table 6.

E3.justification: Reported CFG strengths change between v1 Table 8 and v4 Table 12, including text-generation guidance from 2.5 to 5.75 and both style-transfer strengths from 2.5 to 1.5. v4 also introduces explicit 1/5/20-keyframe comparisons and reduced-task training controls. The principal data-processing and training setup remains intact; these disclosures do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 10 tests whether different task combinations help or hurt relative to specialists, directly extending analysis of the central knowledge-sharing premise. Table 7 adds keyframe-count sensitivity, while Tables 6, 8 and 9 extend component ablations to content recognition accuracy. Existing positional-encoding, curriculum and inference-step studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental results. Both present point estimates.

E6.justification: Table 3 changes MotionLab's FID from 0.223 to 0.167 and R@3 from 0.805 to 0.810. The style-transfer chart changes CRA from 47.86 to 44.62 and SRA from 64.97 to 69.21. Ablation values and specialist rankings change, and substantial keyframe-count, task-combination and CRA results are added. Because guidance settings also change, these are revised reported outcomes rather than established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1-8 retain the same rectified-flow definitions, objective, integration rule and CFG expressions. The curriculum difficulty assumptions are also unchanged; no new formal results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The specialist-performance claim strengthens: v1 Section 6.3 describes broadly comparable outcomes with advantages on particular tasks, whereas v4 claims superiority over specialists on every task and emphasizes specialist-surpassing cross-task learning in the introduction. The central unification paradigm and component contributions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 adds the interpretation that unsuitable task combinations can underperform specialists. It removes v1's finger/facial-motion limitation and the qualification that text generation does not surpass the state of the art. Appendix A also newly claims superiority over CondMDI in all settings, although several one-keyframe metrics in Table 7 favor CondMDI.

D1.justification: v4 newly discloses four days of training and revises the documented guidance hyperparameters. Conversely, its shortened inference-time figure caption omits v1's explicit exclusion of model and data loading. Modality representations, task instructions and the project link are retained.

R1.justification: v4 discusses FLAME alongside MotionCLR as the closest work and credits MoMask for variable frame masking instead of contrasting that choice with MAE. It adds references concerning motion editing, in-betweening and CFG applications, while retaining the overall positioning against task-specific and unified motion systems.

P1.justification: The introduction's explicit contribution list is replaced by an integrated account of modality representation and knowledge sharing. Task-instruction and pre-training explanations are substantially rewritten, the experimental discussion is reorganized, and the appendices are reordered to lead with quantitative results and ablations.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout, extensively resizing and repositioning displays. Figure 1 gains a specialist trace and CRA axis; the in-betweening radar is replaced by a multi-setting table; style-transfer and qualitative ROPE figures move to the appendix. Ablation tables gain CRA columns, and a task-combination table is added.

improvement.justification: The new task-combination and keyframe-count analyses strengthen evaluation of when unification helps. However, v4 removes the explicit finger/facial limitation and claims superiority in every in-betweening setting despite one-keyframe FID of 0.7547 versus CondMDI's 0.1551. Updated reporting is also unreconciled: Table 3 gives FID 0.167 while Figure 7 retains 0.223 at the stated 50 inference steps without explaining the difference. These substantive evidential gains and reporting shortcomings prevent a confident net quality judgment.
